solution.why_others_wrong: 'All carriers' applies when the mother is normal (non-carrier); 'all haemophilic' would need a haemophilic mother; non-carrier daughters are impossible because the father's X always carries the allele.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex-linked inheritance: haemophilia
solution.final_answer: Option D: Half are haemophilic and half are carriers

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a dihybrid is self-pollinated, the F2 always shows the phenotypic ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
Reason (R): Morgan found that when the two genes in a dihybrid cross were situated on the same chromosome, the proportion of parental gene combinations was much higher than that of the non-parental type.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A is false: the 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio is expected only when the two genes assort independently and show complete dominance; linked genes (as in Morgan's Drosophila crosses) give parental combinations far more often, and incomplete dominance changes the ratio. R is true: it is NCERT's account of Morgan's dihybrid crosses in Drosophila, and it is the reason why A cannot hold in every case.
steps: A: false ('always' fails for linked genes or incomplete dominance)
R: true (Morgan: parental combinations predominate for genes on the same chromosome)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes; linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When two genes are tightly linked, the recombinant classes in a test cross greatly outnumber the parental classes.
Statement II: In a test cross of a dihybrid AaBb whose two genes assort independently, the four progeny classes are expected in a 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 ratio.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Statement I is false: tightly linked genes show very low recombination, so the parental classes greatly outnumber the recombinants (Morgan: 1.3% recombination for yellow body and white eye). Statement II is true: an independently assorting dihybrid forms AB, Ab, aB and ab gametes equally, giving 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 with aabb.
steps: Statement I: false, parental types predominate with linkage
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Suppose a polygenic trait is controlled by three genes A, B and C, and each dominant allele adds an equal amount to the phenotype. A plant AaBbCc is crossed with aabbcc. How many phenotypic classes will the progeny show, and what fraction of the progeny will have the same phenotype as the AaBbCc parent?

solution.concept: Additive polygenes in a test cross
solution.explanation: aabbcc contributes no dominant alleles, so each progeny's number of dominant alleles equals the number it gets from AaBbCc: 0, 1, 2 or 3, with probabilities 1/8, 3/8, 3/8, 1/8. With additive effects, phenotype depends only on this number, so there are 4 classes. The AaBbCc parent has 3 dominant alleles; progeny with 3 (genotype AaBbCc) are 1/8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 7 classes and 5/16 belong to the selfed cross AaBbCc × AaBbCc; 3/8 is the fraction with one (or two) dominant alleles; 8 counts genotypes, not additive phenotypes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option B: 4 classes; 1/8

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Both parents are unaffected carriers of phenylketonuria, an autosomal recessive disorder. If they have two children, what is the probability that exactly one of the two children is affected?

solution.explanation: Each child of Aa × Aa is affected (aa) with probability 1/4 and unaffected with 3/4, independently. Exactly one affected can happen in two orders (first affected, second not; or the reverse): 2 × (1/4 × 3/4) = 6/16 = 3/8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/4 is the probability for one child; 3/16 counts only one birth order; 1/16 is the probability that both children are affected.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendelian disorders: phenylketonuria
solution.final_answer: Option A: 3/8

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cross (R round over r wrinkled; Y yellow over y green; independent assortment)) with List-II (phenotypic ratio of the progeny).

List-I:
A. RrYy × Rryy
B. RrYy × rrYY
C. RrYy × RRYy
D. Rryy × rrYy

List-II:
I. 1 : 1 : 1 : 1
II. 3 : 3 : 1 : 1
III. 3 : 1
IV. 1 : 1

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Treat each gene separately and multiply. A: Rr × Rr (3 : 1) and Yy × yy (1 : 1) → 3 : 3 : 1 : 1. B: Rr × rr (1 : 1) and Yy × YY (all yellow) → 1 : 1. C: Rr × RR (all round) and Yy × Yy (3 : 1) → 3 : 1. D: Rr × rr (1 : 1) and yy × Yy (1 : 1) → 1 : 1 : 1 : 1.
solution.shortcut: A gene whose cross gives only one phenotype (Rr × RR, Yy × YY) drops out of the ratio.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes mix up B and C (which gene drops out) or A and D (one 3 : 1 factor versus two 1 : 1 factors).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Genes A and B lie on the same chromosome, with 20 per cent recombination between them. A dihybrid that received Ab from one parent and aB from the other is test-crossed with aabb, giving 1000 progeny. How many progeny of genotype AaBb are expected?

solution.concept: Recombinants depend on the parental combination
solution.explanation: The dihybrid's parental (non-recombinant) gametes are Ab and aB; the recombinant gametes are AB and ab. With 20% recombination, AB and ab together make 20% of the gametes, 10% each. AaBb progeny come from AB gametes: 10% of 1000 = 100. (The parental classes Aabb and aaBb are 400 each.)
solution.why_others_wrong: 400 treats AB as a parental gamete, which it would be only if the dihybrid had received AB and ab; 250 assumes independent assortment; 200 takes the whole recombinant fraction for one class.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option B: 100

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A colour-blind man marries a woman who is homozygous for normal vision. Their daughters later marry men with normal vision. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) All the daughters of the colour-blind man are carriers.
(b) None of the sons of the colour-blind man is colour blind.
(c) About half of the sons born to his daughters are expected to be colour blind.
(d) His sons can pass the allele for colour blindness to their own sons.
(e) About half of the daughters born to his daughters are expected to be colour blind.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Criss-cross inheritance of an X-linked trait
solution.explanation: The man (XᶜY) gives Xᶜ to every daughter and Y to every son; the mother gives only normal X. (a) True: daughters are XXᶜ carriers. (b) True: sons are XY, normal. (c) True: a carrier daughter married to a normal man has sons XᶜY or XY, half colour blind. (d) False: his sons are normal and do not carry the allele; in any case a father gives Y, not X, to his sons. (e) False: granddaughters through a carrier daughter and a normal father always get a normal X from the father, so none is colour blind (half are carriers).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) are wrong; 'b, d and e' also leaves out (a) and (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex-linked inheritance: colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant heterozygous for four independently assorting genes (AaBbCcDd) is self-pollinated. What fraction of the progeny will be heterozygous at all four loci?

solution.explanation: For each gene, Aa × Aa gives 1/4 AA, 1/2 Aa and 1/4 aa, so the chance of being heterozygous at one locus is 1/2. The four genes assort independently, so the probabilities multiply: (1/2)⁴ = 1/16.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/256 uses 1/4 per locus (a homozygous class); 81/256 is the fraction showing all four dominant phenotypes; 1/8 stops at three loci.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: law of independent assortment
solution.final_answer: Option D: 1/16

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A woman with normal phenotype has unaffected parents but a brother with phenylketonuria (an autosomal recessive disorder). She marries a man who is known to be a carrier. What is the probability that their first child will have phenylketonuria?

solution.explanation: The brother is affected (aa), so both unaffected parents are carriers (Aa × Aa). The woman is unaffected, so she is AA or Aa in the ratio 1 : 2, i.e. a carrier with probability 2/3. A child of two carriers is affected with probability 1/4. Overall: 2/3 × 1/4 = 1/6.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/4 assumes the woman is certainly a carrier; 1/8 takes her carrier probability as 1/2 (forgetting that she is known to be unaffected); 2/3 is her probability of being a carrier, not the child's risk.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendelian disorders: phenylketonuria
solution.final_answer: Option B: 1/6

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Of the 64 codons, 3 do not code for any amino acid and function as stop codons. They are:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the codon is a triplet; 61 codons code for amino acids and 3 codons do not code for any amino acid, so they function as stop codons. In the table of codons these are UAA, UAG and UGA.
solution.why_others_wrong: AUG is the initiator codon (methionine); UUU codes for phenylalanine; UGG codes for an amino acid (tryptophan), not a stop signal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option A: UAA, UAG and UGA

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: According to the salient features of the human genome, it contains 3164.7 million nucleotide bases.
Statement II: Chromosome 1 has the fewest genes (231), and the Y chromosome has the most (2968).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Salient features of the human genome
solution.explanation: NCERT: the human genome contains 3164.7 million nucleotide bases (Statement I true). Chromosome 1 has the most genes (2968) and the Y chromosome has the fewest (231); Statement II reverses them, so it is false.
steps: Statement II: false, chromosome 1 has 2968 genes and Y has 231
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project: salient features of the human genome
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (scientist(s)) with List-II (organism used in the experiment).

List-I:
A. Frederick Griffith
B. Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase
C. Meselson and Stahl
D. Taylor and colleagues

List-II:
I. Vicia faba (faba bean)
II. Bacteriophages infecting bacteria
III. Streptococcus pneumoniae
IV. Escherichia coli

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Griffith (1928) worked with Streptococcus pneumoniae (S and R strains) in mice. Hershey and Chase (1952) worked with bacteriophages, viruses that infect bacteria. Meselson and Stahl (1958) grew Escherichia coli in ¹⁵N and ¹⁴N media. Taylor and colleagues (1958) used Vicia faba (faba beans) with radioactive thymidine to show semiconservative replication in chromosomes.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap E. coli with the bacteriophages or with Vicia faba, or give Griffith's bacterium to Meselson and Stahl.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material; replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The Human Genome Project was coordinated by the U.S. Department of Energy and the National Institute of Health.
Statement II: During the early years of the project, the Wellcome Trust (U.K.) became a major partner, and additional contributions came from Japan, France, Germany, China and others.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Organisation of the Human Genome Project
solution.explanation: NCERT: the HGP was a 13-year project coordinated by the U.S. Department of Energy and the National Institute of Health. During the early years, the Wellcome Trust (U.K.) became a major partner; additional contributions came from Japan, France, Germany, China and others. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Adenine and cytosine are both purines.
Statement II: In RNA, uracil is found at the place of thymine.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: nitrogenous bases are of two types: purines (adenine and guanine) and pyrimidines (cytosine, uracil and thymine). So Statement I is false (cytosine is a pyrimidine). Cytosine is common to DNA and RNA, thymine is present in DNA, and uracil is present in RNA at the place of thymine (Statement II true).
steps: Statement I: false, cytosine is a pyrimidine
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): tRNA is called an adapter molecule.
Reason (R): tRNA has an anticodon loop whose bases are complementary to the code, and an amino acid acceptor end to which it binds an amino acid.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: An adapter must read the code on one side and carry the corresponding amino acid on the other. NCERT: tRNA has an anticodon loop with bases complementary to the code, and an amino acid acceptor end to which it binds amino acids. These two features (R) are exactly what make tRNA the adapter between codon and amino acid (A).
steps: Reads the codon + carries the amino acid = adapter: R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code: tRNA, the adapter molecule
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In bacteria, three major types of RNA are needed for protein synthesis. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) mRNA provides the template.
(b) tRNA brings amino acids and reads the genetic code.
(c) rRNA plays a structural and catalytic role during translation.
(d) Each of the three types of RNA is transcribed by a different RNA polymerase.
(e) rRNA carries the codons that specify the sequence of amino acids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in bacteria there are three major types of RNA: mRNA (messenger), tRNA (transfer) and rRNA (ribosomal); all three are needed to synthesise a protein. mRNA provides the template, tRNA brings amino acids and reads the genetic code, and rRNAs play structural and catalytic roles during translation. (d) is false: in bacteria a single DNA-dependent RNA polymerase transcribes all types of RNA. (e) is false: the codons are on mRNA.
steps: (d): false, one RNA polymerase in bacteria
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription unit and the gene
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In bacteria, transcription and translation can be coupled: translation can begin much before the mRNA is fully transcribed.
Reason (R): In bacteria, the mRNA does not require processing to become active, and transcription and translation take place in the same compartment, since there is no separation of cytosol and nucleus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in bacteria, since the mRNA does not require any processing to become active, and since transcription and translation take place in the same compartment (there is no separation of cytosol and nucleus in bacteria), many times the translation can begin much before the mRNA is fully transcribed. Consequently, transcription and translation can be coupled. R gives exactly the reasons for A.
steps: No processing + no nuclear envelope → coupling: R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The inheritance of a character is affected only by the structural gene, and never by the promoter or regulatory sequences.
Statement II: The regulatory sequences of a structural gene are sometimes loosely defined as regulatory genes, even though they do not code for any RNA or protein.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Regulatory sequences and the definition of a gene
solution.explanation: NCERT: the inheritance of a character is also affected by the promoter and regulatory sequences of a structural gene (Statement I false). Hence, sometimes the regulatory sequences are loosely defined as regulatory genes, even though these sequences do not code for any RNA or protein (Statement II true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription unit and the gene
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Which of the following were among the goals of the Human Genome Project?

(a) To store the information obtained in databases.
(b) To improve tools for data analysis.
(c) To transfer related technologies to other sectors, such as industries.
(d) To address the ethical, legal and social issues (ELSI) that may arise from the project.
(e) To sequence the complete genomes of all the non-human organisms on earth.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT lists the goals of the HGP: identify all the approximately 20,000–25,000 genes in human DNA; determine the sequences of the 3 billion base pairs; store this information in databases; improve tools for data analysis; transfer related technologies to other sectors, such as industries; and address the ethical, legal and social issues (ELSI). The genomes of some model organisms (bacteria, yeast, C. elegans, Drosophila, rice, Arabidopsis) were also sequenced, but sequencing all non-human organisms was never a goal.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (e) are wrong; 'a, b and e' also leaves out (c) and (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project: goals of HGP
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A codon in an mRNA reads 5'-AUG-3'. The anticodon of the tRNA that pairs with it, written in the 5'→3' direction, is:

solution.explanation: The anticodon bases are complementary to the codon, and the two pair in antiparallel fashion. Under 5'-A-U-G-3' the anticodon reads 3'-U-A-C-5'. Written 5'→3', it is 5'-CAU-3'.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5'-UAC-3' is the complement written with the wrong polarity; T does not occur in RNA; the anticodon is complementary, not identical, to the codon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code: tRNA, the adapter molecule
solution.final_answer: Option B: 5'-CAU-3'

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The DNA of Escherichia coli is a double helix about 1.36 mm long. Taking the distance between two consecutive base pairs as 0.34 nm, approximately how many base pairs does it contain?

solution.concept: Length of DNA and number of base pairs
solution.explanation: Number of bp = length / distance per bp = (1.36 × 10⁻³ m) / (0.34 × 10⁻⁹ m) = 4 × 10⁶ bp. (NCERT gives the E. coli genome as 4.6 × 10⁶ bp; the round figure here comes from the given length.)
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 × 10³ treats millimetres as metres and nanometres as micrometres (a 10⁻³ slip); 2 × 10⁶ halves the answer for two strands, though the 0.34 nm spacing is already per base pair; 8 × 10⁶ counts nucleotides of both strands, not base pairs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix
solution.final_answer: Option C: 4 × 10⁶

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a double-stranded DNA molecule, 18 per cent of the bases are thymine. What percentage of the bases are guanine?

solution.explanation: In double-stranded DNA, A = T and G = C (Chargaff). T = 18%, so A = 18% and A + T = 36%. The remaining 64% is G + C, shared equally: G = 32%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 18% equates G with T; 64% is G + C together; 82% subtracts only the thymine from 100%.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of DNA: Chargaff's rule
solution.final_answer: Option B: 32 per cent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In every double-stranded DNA, the ratio (A + T)/(G + C) is equal to one.
Statement II: In every double-stranded DNA, the ratio (A + G)/(T + C) is equal to one.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Because a purine always pairs with a pyrimidine (A with T, G with C), A = T and G = C, so purines equal pyrimidines: (A + G)/(T + C) = 1 in every double-stranded DNA (Statement II true). But the amount of A + T relative to G + C differs from one DNA to another, so (A + T)/(G + C) need not be one (Statement I false).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of DNA: Chargaff's rule and base pairing
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the lac operon, the inducer binds directly to the operator, and this allows RNA polymerase to transcribe the structural genes.
Reason (R): In the presence of an inducer such as lactose, the repressor is inactivated by interaction with the inducer, which allows RNA polymerase access to the promoter.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: How the inducer switches on the lac operon
solution.explanation: NCERT: in the absence of an inducer, the repressor (from the i gene) binds to the operator region and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon. In the presence of an inducer such as lactose or allolactose, the repressor is inactivated by interaction with the inducer, which allows RNA polymerase access to the promoter, and transcription proceeds. The inducer acts on the repressor; it is the repressor, not the inducer, that binds the operator. So A is false and R is true.
steps: A: false (the inducer interacts with the repressor; the repressor binds the operator)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (property of the genetic code) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Degenerate
B. Unambiguous and specific
C. Comma-less
D. Nearly universal

List-II:
I. The codon is read in mRNA in a contiguous fashion, without punctuation
II. UUU codes for phenylalanine from bacteria to humans
III. Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon
IV. One codon codes for only one amino acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Degenerate: some amino acids are coded by more than one codon. Unambiguous and specific: one codon codes for only one amino acid. Comma-less: the codon is read in mRNA contiguously, with no punctuation. Nearly universal: from bacteria to humans UUU codes for phenylalanine (some exceptions exist in mitochondrial codons and in some protozoans).
solution.why_others_wrong: The usual confusion is between degenerate (many codons, one amino acid) and unambiguous (one codon, one amino acid), and between comma-less and universal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the action of the bacterial RNA polymerase during transcription are correct?

(a) It uses nucleoside triphosphates as substrates.
(b) Only a short stretch of RNA remains bound to the enzyme during elongation.
(c) Once the polymerase reaches the terminator region, the nascent RNA falls off, and so does the RNA polymerase.
(d) On its own, the RNA polymerase can initiate transcription at the promoter without any initiation factor.
(e) It polymerises nucleotides in a template-independent manner.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: RNA polymerase binds to the promoter and initiates transcription. It uses nucleoside triphosphates as substrate and polymerises in a template-dependent fashion following the rule of complementarity (so (a) is true and (e) false). It also opens the helix and continues elongation; only a short stretch of RNA remains bound to the enzyme (b true). At the terminator, the nascent RNA falls off, and so does the polymerase (c true). The polymerase is only capable of catalysing elongation; it associates transiently with the initiation factor (σ) to initiate (d false).
steps: (d) false: σ factor needed for initiation
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with (d) or (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Compare DNA replication with transcription. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) In both, the new nucleic acid chain is polymerised in the 5'→3' direction.
(b) In transcription, only a segment of DNA and only one of its strands is copied into RNA.
(c) Both processes use deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates as substrates.
(d) Both processes require DNA ligase to join discontinuously synthesised fragments.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: (a) True: DNA-dependent DNA polymerases catalyse polymerisation only in the 5'→3' direction, and RNA is made on the 3'→5' template strand, i.e. also 5'→3'. (b) True: NCERT says that in transcription only a segment of DNA and only one of the strands is copied into RNA. (c) False: replication uses deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates, but RNA polymerase uses (ribo)nucleoside triphosphates. (d) False: DNA ligase joins the discontinuously synthesised fragments of replication; RNA is synthesised continuously.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (d) are wrong; 'a, b and c' adds the false (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication; transcription
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Meselson and Stahl transferred E. coli grown in ¹⁵NH₄Cl into ¹⁴NH₄Cl medium and analysed the DNA after one generation (20 minutes) by CsCl density-gradient centrifugation. If DNA replication had been conservative (both parental strands staying together and both new strands forming a new molecule) instead of semiconservative, what would they have observed after this one generation?

options.text: Equal amounts of hybrid and light DNA
Two bands, one heavy (¹⁵N/¹⁵N) and one light (¹⁴N/¹⁴N), and no hybrid band

solution.concept: Why the Meselson-Stahl result proved semiconservative replication
solution.explanation: Conservative replication would keep the parental ¹⁵N/¹⁵N duplex intact and make an entirely new ¹⁴N/¹⁴N duplex, giving a heavy and a light band after one generation, with no hybrid. What was actually observed after 20 minutes was a single hybrid (intermediate) band, which fits semiconservative replication: each daughter molecule has one old ¹⁵N strand and one new ¹⁴N strand.
steps: Observed: one hybrid band at 20 min → semiconservative
solution.why_others_wrong: A single hybrid band is the actual (semiconservative) result after one generation; equal hybrid and light DNA is the semiconservative result after two generations (40 minutes); a single light band would need all the parental ¹⁵N DNA to disappear.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option D: Two bands, one heavy (¹⁵N/¹⁵N) and one light (¹⁴N/¹⁴N), and no hybrid band

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A mutant E. coli cannot make a functional permease (the y gene is defective), but its i, z and a genes and its promoter and operator are normal. It is placed in a medium containing lactose and no glucose. What happens to the lac operon?

options.text: It is induced normally, because the inducer acts from outside the cell
It is transcribed all the time, because the repressor cannot bind to the operator
It is not induced, because lactose cannot enter the cell to inactivate the repressor
Only the y gene is transcribed, because the other genes have their own promoters

solution.explanation: The lac operon is switched on when lactose (the inducer) enters the cell and inactivates the repressor. NCERT: permease increases the permeability of the cell to β-galactosides, and a very low level of lac operon expression has to be present all the time, otherwise lactose cannot enter the cells. Without functional permease, lactose cannot get in, the repressor stays bound to the operator, and the operon remains switched off.
steps: Repressor stays on operator → operon off
solution.why_others_wrong: The inducer acts inside the cell on the repressor; the repressor and operator here are normal, so expression is not constitutive; z, y and a share one promoter and are transcribed together as one polycistronic unit.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option C: It is not induced, because lactose cannot enter the cell to inactivate the repressor

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If the coding strand of a gene has 30% A, 20% T, 15% G and 35% C, the mRNA transcribed from it will contain 20% uracil.
Statement II: The template strand of the same gene will contain 30% adenine.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Base composition of coding strand, template strand and mRNA
solution.explanation: The mRNA has the same sequence as the coding strand, with U in place of T, so it has 30% A, 20% U, 15% G and 35% C (Statement I true). The template strand is complementary to the coding strand: its A pairs with the coding strand's T, so template A = 20%, T = 30%, G = 35%, C = 15% (Statement II false).
steps: mRNA = coding strand with U for T → U = 20%
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription unit
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text: In a paternity dispute, VNTR bands (in kb) are compared. Child: 1, 3, 5, 7. Mother: 1, 5, 8. Man P: 3, 6, 7. Man Q: 2, 3, 9. Man R: 4, 7, 9. Man S: 1, 5, 6. Assuming every band of the child must come from one of the two biological parents, who could be the father?

solution.explanation: VNTRs are inherited, so each band in the child's fingerprint must come from the mother or the father. The child's bands 1 and 5 are present in the mother. Bands 3 and 7 are not, so they must come from the father. Only man P has both 3 and 7.
steps: Bands to be explained by the father: 3 and 7
solution.why_others_wrong: Q lacks band 7, R lacks band 3, and S shares only the mother's bands and has neither 3 nor 7.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', DNA fingerprinting
solution.final_answer: Option B: Man P

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: An mRNA segment reads 5'-GAUGUUUGGCUAAUG-3'. Translation starts at the first AUG. How many amino acids will be joined into the polypeptide from this segment?

solution.concept: Finding the start and stop codons
solution.explanation: Reading from the first AUG in triplets: AUG (Met) UUU (Phe) GGC (Gly) UAA (stop). Translation ends at the stop codon UAA, which has no tRNA and codes for no amino acid. So three amino acids are joined: Met-Phe-Gly. The final AUG lies after the stop codon and is not translated in this reading.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 counts the stop codon as an amino acid; 5 divides the whole 15-base segment by 3; 2 leaves out methionine coded by the start codon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code; translation
solution.final_answer: Option B: 3

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (change in the coding region of a gene) with List-II (effect on the encoded protein).

List-I:
A. A codon UUU changes to UUC
B. The sixth codon of the β-globin gene changes from GAG to GUG
C. One base is inserted within the gene
D. Three consecutive bases making up one codon are deleted

List-II:
I. The reading frame is shifted from the point of insertion
II. Glutamic acid is replaced by valine
III. One amino acid is lost; the reading frame is unaltered
IV. The same amino acid (phenylalanine) is incorporated

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A: UUU and UUC both code for phenylalanine (degenerate code), so the protein is unchanged. B: GAG → GUG changes glutamic acid to valine at the sixth position of the β-globin chain (sickle-cell anaemia, a point mutation). C: inserting one base shifts the reading frame from that point (frame-shift mutation). D: deleting one whole codon removes one amino acid and leaves the reading frame unaltered from that point onwards.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the silent change with the sickle-cell substitution, or the frame shift (one base) with the in-frame deletion (three bases).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code: mutations and genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Penicillin was used extensively to treat American soldiers wounded in World War II.
Statement II: Fleming, Chain and Florey were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945 for their work on penicillin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: penicillin, discovered by Alexander Fleming and established as an effective antibiotic by Ernest Chain and Howard Florey, was extensively used to treat American soldiers wounded in World War II. Fleming, Chain and Florey were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in industrial products: antibiotics
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Milk turns into curd when lactic acid bacteria (LAB) such as Lactobacillus grow in it.
Reason (R): During their growth, LAB produce acids that coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: micro-organisms such as Lactobacillus, commonly called lactic acid bacteria, grow in milk and convert it to curd. During growth, the LAB produce acids that coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins. The coagulation of milk proteins by these acids (R) is what turns milk into curd (A).
steps: Acid coagulates milk proteins → curd: R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in household products
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the anaerobic sludge digesters of a sewage treatment plant are correct?

(a) The major part of the activated sludge is pumped into the anaerobic sludge digesters.
(b) In the digesters, bacteria that grow anaerobically digest the bacteria and fungi present in the sludge.
(c) The gases produced during this digestion form biogas, which can be used as a source of energy as it is inflammable.
(d) The digesters are kept well aerated by pumping air into them continuously.
(e) The effluent from the settling tank, rather than the sludge, is sent to the digesters.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank as inoculum, and the remaining major part is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters (a true). There, other kinds of bacteria, which grow anaerobically, digest the bacteria and fungi in the sludge (b true). They produce a mixture of methane, hydrogen sulphide and carbon dioxide; these gases form biogas, which can be used as a source of energy as it is inflammable (c true). Air is pumped into the aeration tanks, not the digesters (d false). The effluent from the secondary treatment is generally released into natural water bodies, not into the digesters (e false).
steps: (e): false, the sludge (not the effluent) goes to the digesters
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment: secondary treatment
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (microbe) with List-II (role described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Trichoderma
B. Nucleopolyhedrovirus
C. Glomus
D. Anabaena

List-II:
I. Autotrophic, nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium that is an important biofertiliser in paddy fields
II. Fungus that forms a symbiotic association (mycorrhiza) and absorbs phosphorus for the plant
III. Free-living fungus used as a biological control agent against several plant pathogens
IV. Pathogen that attacks insects and other arthropods, used for species-specific biological control

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Trichoderma species are free-living fungi, very common in root ecosystems, that are effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens. Baculoviruses of the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus attack insects and other arthropods and have species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal applications. Glomus forms mycorrhiza; the fungal symbiont absorbs phosphorus from the soil and passes it to the plant. Anabaena is an autotrophic cyanobacterium that fixes atmospheric nitrogen and is an important biofertiliser in paddy fields.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the two fungi (Trichoderma and Glomus), or the cyanobacterium with the insect virus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents; microbes as biofertilisers
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Under the Ganga Action Plan and the Yamuna Action Plan, it is proposed to build a large number of sewage treatment plants so that only treated sewage may be discharged into the rivers.
Statement II: Biofertilisers are synthetic chemicals that are added to the soil to enrich its nitrogen content.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: River action plans; nature of biofertilisers

Biofertilisers are organisms (bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria) that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil, not synthetic chemicals (Statement II false).
steps: Statement II: false, biofertilisers are organisms
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment; microbes as biofertilisers

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Organic farming and biological control rely on a holistic approach that seeks to understand the webs of interaction between the many organisms that make up the field fauna and flora.
Reason (R): In biological control, the pests of a field are eradicated completely by spraying broad-spectrum chemical pesticides.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

R is false: biocontrol uses biological methods, not chemicals, and the organic farmer does not try to eradicate pests completely, since the beneficial predators and parasites depend on them.
steps: R: false (biocontrol avoids chemicals and does not aim at complete eradication)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
