questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Consider the microbes named in NCERT for various products. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The same yeast species is used both for making bread and for producing alcoholic beverages.
(b) Aspergillus niger and Acetobacter aceti are both fungi.
(c) Streptokinase and lactic acid are both produced by bacteria.
(d) Cyclosporin A and statins are both produced by fungi (Trichoderma polysporum and Monascus purpureus respectively).
(e) Penicillin and citric acid are both produced by bacteria.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Kinds of microbes behind microbial products
solution.explanation: (a) True: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is used as baker's yeast for bread and as brewer's yeast for beverages. (b) False: Aspergillus niger (citric acid) is a fungus but Acetobacter aceti (acetic acid) is a bacterium. (c) True: streptokinase comes from the bacterium Streptococcus and lactic acid from the bacterium Lactobacillus. (d) True: cyclosporin A is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum and statins by the fungus Monascus purpureus. (e) False: penicillin is from the mould Penicillium notatum and citric acid from the fungus Aspergillus niger.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in household products; microbes in industrial products
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A sample of river water just downstream of an outlet discharging untreated sewage is expected to show a higher BOD than a sample of clean river water upstream.
Statement II: The BOD test measures the rate of uptake of oxygen by micro-organisms in a sample of water, and thus indirectly measures the organic matter present in the water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Using BOD as an index of pollution
solution.explanation: Statement II is NCERT's description of the BOD test: it measures the rate of oxygen uptake by micro-organisms, and thus, indirectly, BOD is a measure of the organic matter present. Sewage contains large amounts of organic matter, so water receiving untreated sewage has more organic matter to be oxidised and a higher BOD; the greater the BOD, the greater the polluting potential. Statement I is therefore also true.
steps: Statement II: true (NCERT definition of the test)
Untreated sewage → more organic matter → higher BOD
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lactic acid bacteria improve the nutritional quality of curd by increasing its vitamin B₁₂ content.
Reason (R): In our stomach, lactic acid bacteria play a very beneficial role in checking disease-causing microbes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are NCERT lines about lactic acid bacteria. A is true: LAB increase vitamin B₁₂ and so improve the nutritional quality of curd. R is true: in our stomach LAB check disease-causing microbes. But R describes a different benefit, in the human stomach; checking pathogens is not why curd has more vitamin B₁₂. So R does not explain A.
steps: R is a separate benefit (in the stomach): not the explanation of A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in household products
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The intrinsic rate of natural increase (r) is an important parameter chosen for assessing the impacts of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth.
Statement II: But for predators, prey species could achieve very high population densities and cause ecosystem instability.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Use of r; role of predators
solution.explanation: NCERT: r is an important parameter chosen for assessing impacts of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth (Statement I true). Predators keep prey populations under control; but for predators, prey species could achieve very high population densities and cause ecosystem instability (Statement II true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population growth; population interactions: predation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cuscuta, a parasitic plant commonly found growing on hedge plants, derives its nutrition from the host plant.
Reason (R): In the course of evolution, Cuscuta has lost its chlorophyll and leaves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: Cuscuta, a parasitic plant commonly found growing on hedge plants, has lost its chlorophyll and leaves in the course of evolution, and it derives its nutrition from the host plant which it parasitises. Without chlorophyll and leaves it cannot make its own food (R), which is why it must draw nutrition from the host (A).
steps: No chlorophyll or leaves → cannot photosynthesise → depends on host: R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: parasitism
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A population has attributes, such as birth rate, death rate, sex ratio and age distribution, that an individual organism does not have.
Reason (R): An individual organism also has a birth rate and a death rate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: a population has certain attributes whereas an individual organism does not. An individual may have births and deaths, but a population has birth rates and death rates, expressed per capita; sex ratio and age distribution are also population attributes. So A is true and R is false.
steps: R: false (an individual has births and deaths, not rates)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population attributes
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Orchids show a bewildering diversity of floral patterns. According to NCERT, many of these patterns have evolved to:

options.text: Repel herbivores by mimicking poisonous plants
Attract seed-dispersing birds to the fruits
Reduce water loss from the flowers
Attract the right pollinator insect (bees and bumblebees) and ensure guaranteed pollination

solution.explanation: NCERT: orchids show a bewildering diversity of floral patterns, many of which have evolved to attract the right pollinator insect (bees and bumblebees) and ensure guaranteed pollination by it. Not all orchids offer rewards; Ophrys, for example, uses sexual deceit.
steps: Diverse floral patterns → attract the right pollinator
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT links these patterns to pollinators, not to herbivore defence, seed dispersal or water loss.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: mutualism
solution.final_answer: Option D: Attract the right pollinator insect (bees and bumblebees) and ensure guaranteed pollination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: MacArthur showed that five closely related species of warblers living on the same tree were able to avoid competition and co-exist because of behavioural differences in their foraging activities.
Statement II: Connell's field experiments showed that, on the rocky sea coasts of Scotland, the smaller barnacle Chthamalus excludes the larger barnacle Balanus from the intertidal area.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Statement I is true: MacArthur's warblers co-existed by resource partitioning through differences in foraging behaviour. Statement II is false: Connell found that the larger and competitively superior barnacle Balanus dominates the intertidal area and excludes the smaller Chthamalus from that zone.
steps: Statement II: false, Balanus (larger, superior) excludes Chthamalus
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: competition
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are examples of commensalism described in NCERT?

(a) An orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch
(b) Barnacles growing on the back of a whale
(c) Cattle egrets foraging close to grazing cattle
(d) Clown fish living among the stinging tentacles of a sea anemone
(e) Lichens

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In commensalism one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited. NCERT's examples: an orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch; barnacles on the back of a whale; the cattle egret, which catches the insects flushed out by grazing cattle; and the clown fish, which gets protection from predators among the anemone's stinging tentacles while the anemone does not appear to benefit. Lichens are an example of mutualism (fungus and alga or cyanobacterium).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (e) include a mutualism; '(a), (b) and (c)' leaves out the clown fish.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: commensalism
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In brood parasitism, the host bird incubates the parasitic bird's eggs because they look very different from its own eggs.
Reason (R): During evolution, the eggs of the parasitic bird have come to resemble the host's eggs in size and colour, reducing the chances of the host bird detecting the foreign eggs and ejecting them from the nest.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in brood parasitism (e.g. the cuckoo or koel laying eggs in the crow's nest), the parasitic bird's eggs have evolved to resemble the host's eggs in size and colour, to reduce the chances of the host bird detecting the foreign eggs and ejecting them. So the host incubates them because they look similar, not different: A is false and R is true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: parasitism
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (description) with List-II (expression).

List-I:
A. Exponential growth (rate form)
B. Logistic growth
C. Integral form of exponential growth
D. Change in population density over one time period

List-II:
I. Nₜ = N₀e^(rt)
II. dN/dt = rN
III. N(t+1) = N(t) + [(B + I) − (D + E)]
IV. dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K]

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Exponential growth: dN/dt = rN; its integral form is Nₜ = N₀e^(rt). Logistic (Verhulst-Pearl) growth includes the carrying capacity: dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K]. The density after one period is N(t+1) = N(t) + [(B + I) − (D + E)], since births and immigration add to it and deaths and emigration remove from it.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the rate and integral forms of exponential growth, or the logistic equation with the density-change equation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population growth
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Plants have evolved an astonishing variety of morphological and chemical defences against herbivores.
Reason (R): Unlike animals, plants cannot run away from their predators.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: for plants, herbivores are the predators. The problem is particularly severe for plants because, unlike animals, they cannot run away from their predators; plants therefore have evolved an astonishing variety of morphological (thorns of Acacia and cactus) and chemical (cardiac glycosides of Calotropis; nicotine, caffeine, quinine) defences. R is the reason given for A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: predation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, population ecology is an important area of ecology because it links ecology to:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in nature, we rarely find isolated single individuals; they live in populations. Population ecology is an important area of ecology because it links ecology to population genetics and evolution, since natural selection operates at the population level to evolve the desired traits.
steps: Population ecology ↔ population genetics and evolution
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT does not single out biochemistry, taxonomy or physiology as the fields that population ecology links ecology to.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations
solution.final_answer: Option B: Population genetics and evolution

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT gives the intrinsic rate of natural increase (r) of the human population of India in 1981 as 0.0205 per year. If a population grew exponentially (Nₜ = N₀e^(rt)) at this constant rate, in about how many years would it double? (Take ln 2 = 0.693.)

solution.explanation: Doubling means Nₜ/N₀ = 2 = e^(rt), so rt = ln 2 and t = 0.693/0.0205 ≈ 33.8, i.e. about 34 years.
solution.shortcut: Doubling time ≈ 0.693/r.
solution.why_others_wrong: 49 years is 1/r (ln 2 left out); 3.4 years is a decimal slip; 68 years uses ln 4, the time to quadruple.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: exponential growth
solution.final_answer: Option C: About 34 years

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A plant species is introduced into an island where none of its natural predators or competitors occurs. Based on the examples and principles in NCERT, which of the following statements are reasonable?

(a) Its population may spread rapidly, as the prickly pear cactus did in Australia.
(b) Introducing a predator from its natural habitat may bring it under control.
(c) Native species using the same resources may decline or even become extinct because of competition.
(d) It cannot become invasive, because invasion requires the presence of natural predators.
(e) Its population will grow exponentially for ever, because the resources of an island are unlimited.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: (a) Reasonable: NCERT notes that exotic species introduced into an area become invasive and spread fast because the invaded land lacks their natural predators; the prickly pear cactus in Australia is its example. (b) Reasonable: the cactus was brought under control only after a cactus-feeding predator (a moth) from its natural habitat was introduced. (c) Reasonable: the Abingdon tortoise became extinct within a decade of goats arriving on its island. (d) is the reverse of the truth. (e) is false: no population in nature has unlimited resources, so exponential growth cannot continue indefinitely.
steps: (d): false, absence of predators favours invasion
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: predation and competition; population growth
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For a population growing logistically according to dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K] with K = 1000, the growth rate dN/dt is greater when N = 500 than when N = 900.
Statement II: In the same population, the per capita growth rate is the same when N = 500 and when N = 900.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Growth rate and per capita rate in logistic growth
solution.explanation: At N = 500: dN/dt = r × 500 × 500/1000 = 250r. At N = 900: dN/dt = r × 900 × 100/1000 = 90r. So Statement I is true. The per capita growth rate, (1/N)(dN/dt) = r(K − N)/K, is 0.5r at N = 500 and only 0.1r at N = 900; it falls as N approaches K, so Statement II is false.
steps: Per capita: 0.5r versus 0.1r → Statement II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: logistic growth
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A closed population (no immigration or emigration) of 1000 individuals with a per capita birth rate of 0.05 and a per capita death rate of 0.07 per year is declining.
Statement II: If, during the year, 30 individuals immigrate into this population of 1000 and none emigrate, the population will increase in size.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Statement I: births = 0.05 × 1000 = 50 and deaths = 0.07 × 1000 = 70, so a closed population loses 20 a year: it is declining (true). Statement II: N(t+1) = N(t) + [(B + I) − (D + E)] = 1000 + [(50 + 30) − (70 + 0)] = 1010, an increase (true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population attributes and growth
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Of the incident solar radiation, less than 50 per cent is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR).
Statement II: Low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition, resulting in the build-up of organic materials.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: of the incident solar radiation, less than 50 per cent is photosynthetically active radiation, and plants capture only 2–10 per cent of the PAR (Statement I true). Warm and moist environments favour decomposition, whereas low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit it, resulting in the build-up of organic materials (Statement II true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow; decomposition
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Standing crop
B. Detritus
C. Stratification
D. Species composition

List-II:
I. Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels
II. Identification and enumeration of the plant and animal species of an ecosystem
III. Mass of living material at a trophic level at a particular time
IV. Dead plant remains such as leaves, bark and flowers, and dead remains of animals, including fecal matter

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Standing crop: the mass of living material at a trophic level at a particular time. Detritus: dead plant remains (leaves, bark, flowers) and dead remains of animals, including fecal matter, the raw material for decomposition. Stratification: the vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels (trees, shrubs, herbs and grasses in a forest). Species composition: identification and enumeration of the plant and animal species of an ecosystem.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap standing crop with detritus, or stratification with species composition.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem: structure and function; decomposition; energy flow
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Primary production
B. Gross primary productivity
C. Net primary productivity
D. Secondary productivity

List-II:
I. Rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis
II. Rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers
III. Amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis
IV. Gross primary productivity minus the respiration losses of plants

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: primary production is the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. Gross primary productivity is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. Net primary productivity is GPP minus respiration losses (R) of plants. Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the amount (primary production) with the rate (GPP), or give secondary productivity to producers.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', productivity
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are listed in NCERT as aquatic ecosystems?

(a) Lake
(b) Wetland
(c) Estuary
(d) Grassland
(e) River

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT divides ecosystems into terrestrial and aquatic. Forest, grassland and desert are terrestrial; pond, lake, wetland, river and estuary are aquatic. Crop fields and an aquarium may be considered man-made ecosystems.
steps: Aquatic: pond, lake, wetland, river, estuary
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing (d) includes a terrestrial ecosystem; '(a), (c) and (e)' leaves out the wetland.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem: structure and function
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT states that the annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter, and that the oceans, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, contribute only 55 billion tons of it. Approximately what percentage of the biosphere's annual net primary productivity comes from land?

solution.concept: Contribution of land and oceans to global productivity
solution.explanation: Land contributes 170 − 55 = 115 billion tons. 115/170 × 100 ≈ 67.6 per cent, i.e. about 68 per cent, even though land covers only about 30 per cent of the surface.
solution.why_others_wrong: 32 per cent is the oceans' share; 30 per cent is the land's share of the earth's surface, not of productivity; 70 per cent is the oceans' share of the surface.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', productivity
solution.final_answer: Option D: About 68 per cent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following conditions would slow down the decomposition of detritus?

(a) Detritus rich in lignin
(b) Detritus rich in chitin
(c) Low temperature
(d) Anaerobic conditions in waterlogged soil
(e) A warm and moist environment

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: decomposition is controlled by the chemical composition of detritus and by climatic factors. It is slower when detritus is rich in lignin and chitin and quicker when it is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars. Warm and moist environments favour decomposition, whereas low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit it. So (a)-(d) slow it; (e) speeds it up.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (e) include a condition that favours decomposition; '(a), (c) and (d)' leaves out chitin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', decomposition
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The sun is not the source of energy for the deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystem.
Reason (R): Plants capture only 2–10 per cent of the photosynthetically active radiation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A is true: NCERT says that except for the deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystem, the sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. R is also true, but it concerns how much of the sunlight plants capture in sunlit ecosystems; it says nothing about why a deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystem does not run on solar energy. So R is not the explanation of A.
steps: R is about efficiency of capture, not about the deep sea: not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Grassland P has a gross primary productivity of 20,000 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹, and its plants use 25 per cent of it in respiration. Forest Q has a gross primary productivity of 30,000 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹, and its plants use 60 per cent of it in respiration. Which ecosystem has more biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs, and by how much?

solution.concept: Net primary productivity is what heterotrophs can use
solution.explanation: The biomass available to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers) is the net primary productivity, NPP = GPP − R. P: 20,000 − 5,000 = 15,000. Q: 30,000 − 18,000 = 12,000. P exceeds Q by 3,000 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Q by 10,000' compares GPP instead of NPP; 'Q by 3,000' gets the difference right but the ecosystem wrong; 'P by 13,000' compares respiration losses (18,000 − 5,000).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', productivity
solution.final_answer: Option C: P, by 3,000 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The standing crop of a trophic level is measured as the biomass of living organisms or as their number in a unit area.
Reason (R): For expressing biomass, fresh weight is a more accurate measure than dry weight.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A is true: NCERT says the standing crop is measured as the biomass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area. R is false: the biomass of a species is expressed in terms of fresh or dry weight, but measurement of biomass in terms of dry weight is more accurate.
steps: R: false (dry weight is more accurate)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow; ecological pyramids
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In a food web, grass is eaten by rabbits and grasshoppers; sparrows eat grass seeds and grasshoppers; frogs eat grasshoppers; snakes eat frogs and rabbits; hawks eat snakes and sparrows. Taking producers as the first trophic level, which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The sparrow occupies the second and third trophic levels.
(b) The hawk can occupy the fifth trophic level.
(c) The frog is a primary consumer.
(d) The snake occupies the third and fourth trophic levels.
(e) If the grass disappeared, only the rabbits and grasshoppers would be affected.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Organisms at more than one trophic level
solution.explanation: (a) True: eating seeds, the sparrow is a primary consumer (2nd level); eating grasshoppers, a secondary consumer (3rd). (d) True: snake eating rabbit (2nd) is at the 3rd level; snake eating frog (frog eats grasshopper: 3rd) is at the 4th. (b) True: a hawk eating a snake that ate a frog is at the 5th level (it can also be at the 3rd or 4th via sparrows or rabbit-eating snakes). (c) False: the frog eats herbivorous grasshoppers, so it is a secondary consumer (primary carnivore). (e) False: all consumers depend on producers directly or indirectly.
steps: Loss of grass affects every consumer
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) are wrong; 'b, d and e' also leaves out the sparrow.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow: food chains and trophic levels
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a grazing food chain, the producers fix 20,000 kJ of energy, and only 10 per cent of the energy is transferred from each trophic level to the next. If the top carnivore of the chain receives 2 kJ, at which trophic level is it (taking producers as the first level)?

solution.concept: Using the 10 per cent law to count trophic levels
solution.explanation: Energy falls tenfold at each step: 20,000 (1st, producers) → 2,000 (2nd) → 200 (3rd) → 20 (4th) → 2 (5th). So the top carnivore is at the fifth trophic level. This rapid fall is why the number of trophic levels in a grazing food chain is restricted.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Fourth' counts the transfers (4) instead of the levels; 'sixth' adds one level too many; 'third' would receive 200 kJ.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow: 10 per cent law
solution.final_answer: Option A: Fifth

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Because of the 10 per cent law of energy transfer, the pyramid of biomass of every ecosystem must be upright.
Reason (R): The pyramid of energy is always upright, because some energy is always lost as heat at each step of energy flow from one trophic level to the next.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Biomass and energy pyramids can differ
solution.explanation: A is false: the pyramid of biomass in a sea is generally inverted, because the biomass of fishes far exceeds that of phytoplankton; energy transfer rules do not fix the standing biomass at any moment. R is true: NCERT says the pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted, because some energy is always lost as heat at each step.
steps: A: false (inverted biomass pyramid in a sea)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecological pyramids
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Since less than 50 per cent of the incident solar radiation is PAR, and plants capture only 2–10 per cent of the PAR, plants capturing 2 per cent of the PAR fix less than 1 per cent of the incident solar radiation.
Statement II: Because producers fix such a small fraction of the incident radiation, they form the narrowest bar of the pyramid of energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Small capture of sunlight versus the shape of the energy pyramid
solution.explanation: Statement I: 2% of less than 50% is less than 1% of the incident radiation (true). Statement II is false: the pyramid of energy compares the energy present at successive trophic levels, not the energy fixed compared with sunlight. Producers hold the most energy of any trophic level and form the widest bar at the base; the bars narrow towards the top carnivores, and the pyramid is always upright.
steps: Producers form the base (widest bar) → Statement II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow; ecological pyramids
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

B. Extinction of more than 200 species of cichlid fish in Lake Victoria
C. Clearing of the Amazon rain forest for soya bean cultivation and cattle grazing

The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria (an alien species invasion) led to the extinction of more than 200 species of cichlid fish. Clearing the Amazon forest for soya beans and beef cattle is habitat loss. When a host fish species becomes extinct, its unique assemblage of parasites also meets the same fate: co-extinction.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', loss of biodiversity: causes of biodiversity losses

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Species richness follows log S = log C + Z log A. Take Z = 0.1 for areas within a region and Z = 1.0 for very large areas such as whole continents (both within NCERT's ranges). When the area studied increases tenfold, by about what factor does species richness increase in each case?

options.text: About 1.26 times within a region, but 10 times at the continental scale
10 times within a region, but about 1.26 times at the continental scale
About 1.1 times within a region, but 2 times at the continental scale

solution.explanation: From the equation, S₂/S₁ = (A₂/A₁)^Z. For a tenfold area increase: within a region, 10^0.1 ≈ 1.26; at the continental scale, 10^1.0 = 10. NCERT notes that Z lies between 0.1 and 0.2 within a region but is much steeper (0.6 to 1.2) for very large areas such as entire continents.
solution.why_others_wrong: '1.26 in both' ignores the steeper continental slope; the third option swaps the two cases; 1.1 and 2 come from adding Z to 1 instead of raising 10 to the power Z.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', patterns of biodiversity: species-area relationships
solution.final_answer: Option B: About 1.26 times within a region, but 10 times at the continental scale

solution.explanation: NCERT: animals without a body cavity are acoelomates, e.g. platyhelminthes (Taenia, the tapeworm). In pseudocoelomates the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, e.g. aschelminthes (Ancylostoma, the hookworm). Coelomates have a true coelom lined by mesoderm, e.g. annelids (Hirudinaria, the blood-sucking leech).
solution.shortcut: Flat → none; round → pseudo; ringed → true coelom.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps the flatworm and the roundworm; B puts the coelomate leech first; C swaps the leech and the hookworm.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', basis of classification: coelom
solution.final_answer: Option D: Taenia, Ancylostoma, Hirudinaria

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following pairs consist of two animals belonging to the same class?

(a) Naja and Chelone
(b) Aptenodytes and Struthio
(c) Ichthyophis and Hippocampus
(d) Pteropus and Neophron
(e) Petromyzon and Myxine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Naja (cobra) and Chelone (turtle) are both reptiles; Aptenodytes (penguin) and Struthio (ostrich) are both birds; Petromyzon (lamprey) and Myxine (hagfish) are both cyclostomes. Ichthyophis is a limbless amphibian while Hippocampus (sea horse) is a bony fish; Pteropus (flying fox) is a mammal while Neophron (vulture) is a bird.
solution.why_others_wrong: B and D include (c); C includes (d); B and C also leave out a true pair.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', subphylum Vertebrata: classes
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sharks such as Scoliodon have to swim constantly to avoid sinking, whereas bony fishes such as Labeo need not.
Reason (R): Bony fishes have an air bladder that regulates buoyancy, while cartilaginous fishes do not have an air bladder.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Air bladder and buoyancy in fishes
solution.explanation: NCERT: in Chondrichthyes the air bladder is absent, and due to this they have to swim constantly to avoid sinking. In Osteichthyes an air bladder is present which regulates buoyancy. The presence or absence of the air bladder is therefore the direct cause of the contrast stated in A.
steps: Air bladder absent → must swim to stay afloat; present → buoyancy regulated
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because NCERT itself gives the absence of the air bladder as the reason for constant swimming; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', classes Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (animal) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Aurelia
B. Ctenoplana
C. Ascaris

List-II:
I. Body cavity not lined by mesoderm (pseudocoelom)
II. True coelom with metameric segmentation
III. Umbrella-shaped, free-swimming medusa
IV. Eight external rows of ciliated comb plates

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Aurelia (jelly fish) is the NCERT example of the umbrella-shaped, free-swimming medusa. Ctenoplana is a ctenophore, with eight external rows of ciliated comb plates. Ascaris is an aschelminth, a pseudocoelomate. Pheretima (earthworm) is an annelid: a coelomate showing metameric segmentation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
An invertebrate has a chitinous exoskeleton, jointed appendages and Malpighian tubules for excretion. Which of the following would NCERT also lead you to expect in it?

(a) Its body consists of head, thorax and abdomen.
(b) Statocysts or balance organs are present among its sensory organs.
(c) Nephridia help in its osmoregulation and excretion.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Recognising an arthropod and its features
solution.explanation: A chitinous exoskeleton, jointed appendages and Malpighian tubules mark the animal as an arthropod. NCERT: the arthropod body consists of head, thorax and abdomen; sensory organs like antennae, eyes and statocysts (balance organs) are present; arthropods are mostly oviparous; their circulatory system is of the open type. Nephridia are the excretory organs of annelids, not arthropods.
solution.why_others_wrong: A includes (c); C includes (e) and leaves out (a); D includes both false statements.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In which of the following pairs do the two animals show the same type of body symmetry as adults?

solution.concept: Symmetry as a basis of classification
solution.explanation: NCERT: sponges are mostly asymmetrical; coelenterates, ctenophores and adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical; annelids, platyhelminthes and arthropods are bilaterally symmetrical. Antedon (sea lily, an echinoderm) is radial as an adult, and Aurelia (a coelenterate) is radial too.
solution.why_others_wrong: Spongilla is a sponge (mostly asymmetrical) while Ctenoplana is radial; Nereis is bilateral while Echinus is radial as an adult; Taenia is bilateral while Adamsia is radial.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the male frog, the vasa efferentia arise from the testes and enter the kidneys. According to NCERT, how many vasa efferentia are there?

solution.concept: Male reproductive system of the frog
solution.explanation: NCERT: vasa efferentia are 10–12 in number; they arise from the testes, enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder's canal, which finally communicates with the urinogenital duct opening into the cloaca.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other numbers are not given by NCERT for the vasa efferentia of the frog.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option B: 10–12

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In multicellular animals, a group of similar cells along with intercellular substances that performs a specific function is called a(n):

solution.explanation: NCERT: a group of similar cells along with intercellular substances perform a specific function, and such an organisation is called a tissue. Tissues organised in a specific proportion and pattern form an organ, and organs with a common function form an organ system.
steps: Similar cells + intercellular substance + one function → tissue
solution.why_others_wrong: An organ is made of tissues arranged in a pattern; an organ system is a group of organs; a gland is only one kind of specialised epithelial structure.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues
solution.final_answer: Option A: Tissue

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Besides a closed blood vascular system, the frog has a lymphatic system. According to NCERT, the lymph of the frog differs from its blood in that lymph:

options.text: Lacks a few proteins and the RBCs

solution.explanation: NCERT: frogs have a well-developed closed type of circulatory system and also a lymphatic system. Lymph is different from blood: it lacks a few proteins and RBCs.
steps: Lymph = blood minus a few proteins and the RBCs
solution.why_others_wrong: Lymph is a fluid with a plasma-like base, so it does not lack plasma; it lacks RBCs rather than having more of them; NCERT does not say that it lacks WBCs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: circulatory system
solution.final_answer: Option D: Lacks a few proteins and the RBCs

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the frog, bile emulsifies fat, and the pancreatic juices digest carbohydrates and proteins.
Statement II: In the frog, the final digestion of food takes place in the stomach.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in the frog, food is digested in the stomach by HCl and gastric juices, and the partially digested food (chyme) passes to the duodenum. Bile emulsifies fat and pancreatic juices digest carbohydrates and proteins. Final digestion takes place in the intestine, not in the stomach.
steps: Statement II → false (final digestion in the intestine)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept that final digestion is in the stomach; B rejects the NCERT roles of bile and pancreatic juice.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: digestive system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Frogs are cold-blooded (poikilotherm) animals, whose body temperature varies with the temperature of the environment.
Reason (R): Frogs have the ability to change their colour to hide from their enemies.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Poikilothermy and protective coloration in the frog
solution.explanation: NCERT states both: frogs are cold-blooded or poikilotherm animals, i.e. their body temperature varies with the temperature of the environment; and frogs have the ability to change colour to hide from their enemies (camouflage, a protective coloration called mimicry). Colour change is a defence against enemies; it is not why the body temperature follows the environment.
steps: R is about protection from enemies, a different property → B
solution.why_others_wrong: A would make colour change the cause of poikilothermy, which NCERT does not say; C and D reject statements that NCERT makes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: morphology
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the neural system of the frog are correct?

(a) It is organised into a central neural system, a peripheral neural system and an autonomic neural system.
(b) The peripheral neural system consists of the cranial nerves and the spinal nerves.
(c) The autonomic neural system consists of the sympathetic and the parasympathetic neural systems.
(d) The brain is enclosed in a cartilaginous brain box.
(e) The spinal cord is enclosed in the vertebral column.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the frog's neural system is organised into a central neural system (brain and spinal cord), a peripheral neural system (cranial and spinal nerves) and an autonomic neural system (sympathetic and parasympathetic). The brain is enclosed in a bony structure called the brain box (cranium), and the spinal cord is enclosed in the vertebral column.
solution.why_others_wrong: A and C include the false (d); B leaves out the true (a); A also leaves out (c) and (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: neural system
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (role).

List-I:
A. Tight junctions
B. Adhering junctions
C. Gap junctions
D. Fibroblasts

List-II:
I. Perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together
II. Produce and secrete fibres
III. Help stop substances from leaking across a tissue
IV. Connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions and small molecules

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue; adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together; gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules. Areolar tissue contains fibroblasts, the cells that produce and secrete fibres.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps tight and adhering junctions; B swaps adhering and gap junctions; D swaps tight and gap junctions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', epithelial tissue: cell junctions; loose connective tissue
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Bones interact with the skeletal muscles attached to them to bring about movements.
Statement II: Bones support and protect the softer tissues and organs of the body.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: bones support and protect softer tissues and organs. Limb bones such as the long bones of the legs serve weight-bearing functions, and they also interact with the skeletal muscles attached to them to bring about movements. Both statements are true.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT descriptions of bone, so B, C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', connective tissue: specialised connective tissue (bone)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When two or more organs perform a common function by their physical and/or chemical interaction, they together form an organ system.
Statement II: In unicellular organisms, functions such as digestion, respiration and reproduction are performed by different tissues.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in unicellular organisms, all functions like digestion, respiration and reproduction are performed by a single cell; in multicellular animals the same functions are carried out by different groups of cells. When two or more organs perform a common function by their physical and/or chemical interaction, they together form an organ system, e.g. the digestive and respiratory systems.
steps: Statement II → false (a single cell does everything; there are no tissues)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept that unicellular organisms have tissues; B rejects the NCERT definition of an organ system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', introduction and animal tissues
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of BOTH smooth muscle and cardiac muscle, as described in NCERT?

options.text: Both are closely attached to skeletal bones
Both are found in the walls of the stomach and intestine
Both are the striated muscle of the biceps

solution.explanation: NCERT: smooth muscles are involuntary, as their functioning cannot be directly controlled; they occur in the walls of internal organs such as blood vessels, stomach and intestine. Cardiac muscle is a contractile tissue present only in the heart and is also involuntary. Skeletal muscle is closely attached to skeletal bones, as in the biceps.
solution.why_others_wrong: Attachment to skeletal bones and the biceps describe skeletal muscle; cardiac muscle is present only in the heart, not in the walls of the stomach and intestine.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', muscle tissue
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both are involuntary

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Suppose a dye injected into a testis of a male frog were carried along with the sperms. Which route would it follow to reach the outside?

options.text: Testis → vasa efferentia → Bidder's canal in the kidney → oviduct → cloaca
Testis → urinogenital duct → vasa efferentia → kidney → cloaca
Testis → separate vas deferens → cloacal aperture, bypassing the kidney
Testis → vasa efferentia → Bidder's canal in the kidney → urinogenital duct → cloaca

solution.concept: Route of sperms in the male frog
solution.explanation: NCERT: the vasa efferentia arise from the testes, enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder's canal. This finally communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidneys and opens into the cloaca, a small median chamber used to pass faecal matter, urine and sperms to the exterior.
solution.why_others_wrong: A ends in an oviduct, which belongs to the female; B puts the urinogenital duct before the vasa efferentia; C invents a separate vas deferens, whereas sperms pass through the kidney.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option D: Testis → vasa efferentia → Bidder's canal in the kidney → urinogenital duct → cloaca

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A tissue has cells lying in spaces called lacunae, and a very hard, non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres. In an adult human, at which of the following sites would this tissue be found?

solution.explanation: NCERT: bone has a very hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres, and the bone cells (osteocytes) lie in spaces called lacunae. Limb bones, such as the long bones of the legs, serve weight-bearing functions. The tip of the nose has cartilage (solid but pliable matrix), tendons are dense regular connective tissue, and the skin has dense irregular connective tissue.
steps: Bone → long bones of the legs
solution.why_others_wrong: The tip of the nose is supported by cartilage, whose matrix is pliable; tendons and the skin have collagen-rich dense connective tissue without calcium salts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', connective tissue: specialised connective tissue
solution.final_answer: Option A: Long bones of the legs

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Suppose that in a person's heart, the communication junctions (intercalated discs) at the fusion points between cardiac muscle cells failed to function, though the cells still stuck together. According to NCERT, which property would be lost?

options.text: The involuntary nature of the cardiac muscle
The presence of cardiac muscle only in the heart
The ability of the cells to contract as a unit
The striations of skeletal muscle fibres

solution.explanation: NCERT: cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells and make them stick together. Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit, i.e. when one cell receives a signal to contract, its neighbours are also stimulated to contract.
steps: Intercalated discs → signal passes to neighbouring cells
Lost → cells cannot contract as a unit
solution.why_others_wrong: Being involuntary and being present only in the heart do not depend on the communication junctions; skeletal muscle fibres are a different tissue altogether.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', muscle tissue: cardiac muscle
solution.final_answer: Option C: The ability of the cells to contract as a unit

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
NCERT classifies connective tissues as loose, dense and specialised. Which of the following are specialised connective tissues?

(a) Cartilage
(b) Bone
(c) Blood
(d) Adipose tissue
(e) Tendon

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: connective tissues are loose (areolar and adipose tissue), dense (dense regular – tendons and ligaments; dense irregular – skin) and specialised (cartilage, bones and blood).
solution.shortcut: Specialised connective tissues = cartilage, bone, blood.
solution.why_others_wrong: A leaves out blood, a fluid specialised connective tissue; B adds adipose tissue, which is loose connective tissue; C adds adipose tissue and tendon and leaves out cartilage and bone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', connective tissue
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An enzyme shows its highest activity at pH 2. If the pH of its medium is raised to 7, keeping all other conditions the same, its activity is expected to:

options.text: Decline, because activity falls on either side of the optimum pH
Rise, because a neutral pH suits all enzymes
Remain unchanged, because pH affects only inorganic catalysts
Rise first and then become constant at Vmax

solution.explanation: NCERT: each enzyme shows its highest activity at a particular pH, its optimum pH, and activity declines both below and above the optimum value. Moving from pH 2 to pH 7 takes the enzyme away from its optimum, so its activity falls.
solution.why_others_wrong: Enzymes do not share one optimum pH; pH does affect enzymes (changes can alter their tertiary structure); Vmax describes the effect of substrate concentration, not of pH.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: factors affecting enzyme activity
solution.final_answer: Option A: Decline, because activity falls on either side of the optimum pH

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Glucose and ribose, two sugars found in the acid-soluble pool of living tissues, are respectively a:

solution.explanation: Glucose is a six-carbon sugar (hexose); ribose is a five-carbon sugar (pentose). NCERT shows both among the sugars of the acid-soluble pool, and states that the sugar in polynucleotides is either ribose or 2′-deoxyribose.
solution.why_others_wrong: A reverses the two; B and D give both sugars the same number of carbons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', how to analyse chemical composition (sugars); nucleic acids
solution.final_answer: Option C: Hexose and pentose

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A lipid from a cell membrane yields, on hydrolysis, glycerol, fatty acids, phosphoric acid and a phosphorylated organic compound. According to NCERT, it is a:

options.text: Saturated fatty acid, such as palmitic acid

solution.explanation: NCERT: some lipids have phosphorous and a phosphorylated organic compound in them; these are phospholipids, found in the cell membrane. Lecithin is one example.
steps: Phosphorus + phosphorylated organic compound + membrane → phospholipid
solution.why_others_wrong: A triglyceride is glycerol esterified with three fatty acids, with no phosphorus; palmitic acid is a single fatty acid; cellulose is a polysaccharide of glucose, not a lipid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', lipids
solution.final_answer: Option B: Phospholipid, such as lecithin

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An enzyme breaks the glycosidic bonds of starch by adding water, releasing glucose. In the NCERT classification of enzymes, it belongs to the class:

solution.explanation: NCERT: hydrolases are enzymes catalysing the hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, C–C, C–halide or P–N bonds. Breaking glycosidic bonds of starch with water is hydrolysis.
solution.why_others_wrong: Lyases remove groups by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds; ligases link two compounds together; isomerases inter-convert isomers.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', classification and nomenclature of enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option D: Hydrolases

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following proteins would NOT show a quaternary structure?

options.text: A protein made of a single polypeptide chain
A protein assembled from four separately folded subunits
A protein made of two α and two β subunits

solution.explanation: NCERT: some proteins are an assembly of more than one polypeptide or subunit, and the manner in which these individually folded polypeptides are arranged with respect to each other is the quaternary structure. A protein of a single polypeptide chain has no subunits to arrange.
steps: Quaternary structure needs two or more subunits
solution.why_others_wrong: Haemoglobin (two α and two β subunits) and any four-subunit protein are assemblies of polypeptides, so they show a quaternary structure.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', structure of proteins
solution.final_answer: Option A: A protein made of a single polypeptide chain

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A purified protein loses its biological activity after mild heating, although none of its peptide bonds is broken. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) Its primary structure is unchanged.
(b) Its three-dimensional (tertiary) structure has been altered.
(c) Heat can denature proteins.
(d) The sequence of its amino acids has changed.
(e) Mild heating hydrolyses the peptide bonds of every protein.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Levels of protein structure and denaturation
solution.explanation: The primary structure is the sequence of amino acids joined by peptide bonds; since no peptide bond is broken, it is intact. NCERT: the tertiary structure is absolutely necessary for many biological activities of proteins, and high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat. Loss of activity with intact peptide bonds means the three-dimensional folding has changed.
solution.why_others_wrong: A leaves out (c); B and D include (d), which cannot be true when no peptide bond is broken; D also includes (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', structure of proteins; factors affecting enzyme activity
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a potential-energy diagram of an uncatalysed reaction S → P, the substrate S is at 40 kJ mol⁻¹, the transition state at 110 kJ mol⁻¹ and the product P at 15 kJ mol⁻¹ (hypothetical values). Using the NCERT definition, the activation energy of this reaction is:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the difference in average energy content of S from that of the transition state is called the activation energy. Here it is 110 − 40 = 70 kJ mol⁻¹. (P lies below S, so the reaction is exothermic, but S must still pass through the higher-energy transition state.)
solution.why_others_wrong: 95 measures from the product instead of the substrate; 25 is the energy difference between S and P; 110 is the energy of the transition state itself, not a difference.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: how do enzymes bring about such high rates of chemical conversions?
solution.final_answer: Option B: 70 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: An endothermic reaction is an energy-requiring reaction.
Statement II: In an endothermic reaction, the product is at a lower energy level than the substrate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT contrasts the exothermic (spontaneous) reaction with the endothermic, energy-requiring reaction. If the product P is at a lower level than the substrate S, the reaction is exothermic and energy need not be supplied to form the product. So a product below the substrate describes an exothermic, not an endothermic, reaction.
steps: Statement II → false (that describes an exothermic reaction)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept Statement II, which describes an exothermic reaction; B rejects NCERT's description of an endothermic reaction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: how do enzymes bring about such high rates of chemical conversions?
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A human enzyme stored at 4 °C for a day can catalyse its reaction again when it is brought back to 37 °C.
Reason (R): Low temperature preserves an enzyme in a temporarily inactive state.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Effect of low temperature on enzymes
solution.explanation: NCERT: low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state, whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat. Because the cold only inactivates the enzyme temporarily, warming it back to its working temperature restores its activity.
steps: Inactivation is temporary → activity returns → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because the temporary nature of cold inactivation is exactly why activity returns; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: factors affecting enzyme activity
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (compound) with List-II (category).

List-I:
A. Thymine
B. Guanine
C. Adenosine
D. Cytidylic acid

List-II:
I. Nucleotide
II. Nucleoside
III. Substituted purine
IV. Substituted pyrimidine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: adenine and guanine are substituted purines, while uracil, cytosine and thymine are substituted pyrimidines. A nitrogen base attached to a sugar is a nucleoside (adenosine, guanosine, thymidine, uridine, cytidine); when a phosphate group is also esterified to the sugar, it is a nucleotide (adenylic, thymidylic, guanylic, uridylic and cytidylic acids).
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps the purine and the pyrimidine; B swaps the nucleoside and the nucleotide; C makes both swaps.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A compound from the acid-insoluble fraction of a tissue yields, on complete hydrolysis, a pentose sugar, phosphoric acid and heterocyclic nitrogenous bases. The compound is most likely a:

solution.explanation: NCERT: nucleic acids are polynucleotides, found in the acid-insoluble fraction. Each nucleotide has three chemically distinct components: a heterocyclic compound (nitrogenous base), a monosaccharide (ribose or 2′-deoxyribose, both pentoses) and a phosphoric acid or phosphate.
steps: Acid-insoluble polymer of nucleotides → nucleic acid
solution.why_others_wrong: A phospholipid yields glycerol and fatty acids, not heterocyclic bases and a pentose; a nucleoside has no phosphate and is a small acid-soluble molecule; a protein yields amino acids.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids
solution.final_answer: Option B: Nucleic acid

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An enzyme that moves a hydrogen atom from a substrate S to another substrate S′ is not placed in the class Transferases.
Reason (R): In NCERT's classification, transferases catalyse the transfer of a group G, other than hydrogen, between a pair of substrates S and S′.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT defines transferases as enzymes catalysing the transfer of a group G (other than hydrogen) between a pair of substrates S and S′. Transfer of hydrogen between S and S′ is an oxido-reduction, catalysed by oxidoreductases (dehydrogenases). The exclusion of hydrogen in the definition is exactly why such an enzyme is not a transferase.
steps: Hydrogen is excluded from 'group G' → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because the definition in R is what excludes the enzyme; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', classification and nomenclature of enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: For a reaction S → P (hypothetical values), the substrate lies at 30 kJ mol⁻¹ and the product at 10 kJ mol⁻¹. Without an enzyme the transition state lies at 105 kJ mol⁻¹; with the enzyme it lies at 70 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the activation energy with the enzyme, and by how much has the enzyme lowered it?

options.text: Ea = 60 kJ mol⁻¹; lowered by 35 kJ mol⁻¹
Ea = 70 kJ mol⁻¹; lowered by 35 kJ mol⁻¹
Ea = 40 kJ mol⁻¹; lowered by 75 kJ mol⁻¹
Ea = 40 kJ mol⁻¹; lowered by 35 kJ mol⁻¹

solution.explanation: NCERT: activation energy is the difference in energy between the substrate S and the transition state; an enzyme brings down this energy barrier, making the transition of S into P easier. Without the enzyme, Ea = 105 − 30 = 75 kJ mol⁻¹; with it, Ea = 70 − 30 = 40 kJ mol⁻¹. The lowering is 75 − 40 = 35 kJ mol⁻¹. The energies of S and P are not changed by the enzyme.
solution.shortcut: Lowering = difference between the two transition-state energies = 105 − 70 = 35.
solution.why_others_wrong: A measures the new Ea from the product (70 − 10); B takes the transition-state energy itself as Ea; C gives the uncatalysed Ea (75) as the lowering.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: how do enzymes bring about such high rates of chemical conversions?
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ea = 40 kJ mol⁻¹; lowered by 35 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
An enzyme catalyses the reaction S reduced + S′ oxidised → S oxidised + S′ reduced, and it is catalytically active only when the co-enzyme NAD is present. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The enzyme is an oxidoreductase (dehydrogenase).
(b) The co-enzyme NAD contains the vitamin niacin.
(c) NAD is the protein part (apoenzyme) of this enzyme.
(d) If NAD is removed, the enzyme loses its catalytic activity.
(e) The enzyme is a transferase, because a group moves from S to S′.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: oxidoreductases/dehydrogenases catalyse oxido-reduction between two substrates, S reduced + S′ oxidised → S oxidised + S′ reduced. Co-factors are non-protein constituents; the protein portion is the apoenzyme. The essential chemical components of many co-enzymes are vitamins – NAD and NADP contain niacin. When the co-factor is removed, the catalytic activity of the enzyme is lost. Transferases move a group other than hydrogen, so this redox enzyme is not a transferase.
steps: (c) false – co-enzymes are non-protein; apoenzyme is the protein
(e) false – redox transfer of hydrogen is not a transferase reaction
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D include (c); C includes (e) and leaves out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', classification and nomenclature of enzymes; co-factors
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
On complete hydrolysis, compound X gives only glucose and has a branched chain; compound Y gives only fructose; compound Z gives one glycerol and three fatty acid molecules. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) X could be glycogen.
(b) Y could be inulin.
(c) Z is a triglyceride.
(d) X is a heteropolymer.
(e) Z is a macromolecule of molecular weight above ten thousand daltons.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Glycogen, the animal store of energy, is a branched polymer of glucose, i.e. a homopolymer. NCERT: inulin is a polymer of fructose. Glycerol esterified with three fatty acids is a triglyceride. Lipids have molecular weights not exceeding 800 Da and are not strictly macromolecules.
steps: (d) false – one kind of monomer → homopolymer
solution.why_others_wrong: A leaves out (c); B includes (d); D includes (e) and leaves out (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides; lipids
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Two proteins contain exactly the same numbers of each kind of amino acid, yet they have different shapes and functions. In which feature must they differ at the most basic level?

options.text: The kinds of amino acids present in them
The total number of amino acids in each
The type of bond joining adjacent amino acids, peptide in one and glycosidic in the other
The sequence of amino acids, i.e. their primary structure

solution.explanation: NCERT: proteins are linear chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds, and the sequence of amino acids – the positional information of which amino acid is first, second and so on – is the primary structure. With the same composition, only the order can differ, and the higher levels of folding follow from the chain.
steps: Same kinds and numbers → composition identical
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B are ruled out by the stem (same kinds and numbers); every protein's amino acids are joined by peptide bonds, so C is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', proteins; structure of proteins
solution.final_answer: Option D: The sequence of amino acids, i.e. their primary structure

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A tissue containing nucleotides, nucleosides, free amino acids, DNA and proteins is ground in trichloroacetic acid and strained through cheesecloth. Which set will be found in the filtrate (acid-soluble pool)?

options.text: Nucleotides, nucleosides and free amino acids

solution.explanation: NCERT: grinding a tissue in trichloroacetic acid and straining it gives an acid-soluble filtrate containing micromolecules (molecular weights below one thousand daltons) such as amino acids, sugars, nucleosides and nucleotides, and an acid-insoluble retentate containing macromolecules such as proteins, polysaccharides and nucleic acids.
steps: Small molecules → filtrate: nucleotides, nucleosides, amino acids
solution.why_others_wrong: DNA and proteins are macromolecules of the acid-insoluble retentate, so B, C and D each place a macromolecule in the filtrate or leave the small molecules out.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', how to analyse chemical composition
solution.final_answer: Option A: Nucleotides, nucleosides and free amino acids

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A worker who spent many years in a stone-breaking unit without any protection develops serious lung damage. According to NCERT, what is the most likely cause, and how could it have been prevented?

options.text: Allergic inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles; by avoiding pollen
Inflammation due to long exposure to dust, leading to fibrosis; by wearing a protective mask
Damage to the alveolar walls by cigarette smoke; by quitting smoking
Failure of the respiratory rhythm centre; by keeping the body cool

solution.explanation: NCERT: in industries involving grinding or stone-breaking, so much dust is produced that the defence mechanism of the body cannot fully cope. Long exposure can give rise to inflammation leading to fibrosis (proliferation of fibrous tissues) and thus serious lung damage. Workers in such industries should wear protective masks.
solution.why_others_wrong: A describes asthma; C describes emphysema, whose major cause NCERT gives as cigarette smoking; D is not an occupational disorder at all.
